messages.author: f5c791567876cfd5
messages.subject: Using AR function with a list
parts:
Hi everyone,

That's my third post in one month, sorry to spam the forum!
argument?.
I want to use the function AR with a list of audio files in .wav. My list is huge (300+ elements) so I can't do it by hand. However, the function AR seems to not accept the list as arguments. When I try the function with a list of 2 arguments (i. e. "AR(list)"), I receive the following error:
Error in inputw(wave = wave, f = f) : 
  argument "f" is missing, with no default
In addition: Warning message:
In AR(list) :
  Computing the AR index on a single object does not make a lot of sense as AR is a ranked index

Maybe the problem is due to the fact that I don't add the f argument in the AR function, but I execute it like that ("AR(list, f=256000)"), I have the same error. Morevoer, when I do it with the two elements separately (i. e. "AR(wave1,wave2)") that works.

For information, my list looks like that:

Thank you again for your help!

Jeremy

messages.author: 1f04514119422e67
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Using AR function with a list
parts:
Indeed, the function does not accept a list. As per the help file, it accepts only sound objects, or paths to sound files:
Arguments
… Wave, WaveMC, audioSample objects if datatype="objects", or a path as a character string to a directory including .wav and/or .mp3 files if datatype="files"

A list of sound objects is not a sound object, this distinction is important. If your list is composed of audio files, you can pass the path of the directory/folder containg those files to the function (something like "c:/users/you/files/" . careful with the quotation marks and the slashes), wich will read them and perform the necessary calculations.
see the examples in the help files to see how you use the files path instead of the objects

parts:
the last example, the one that uses getwd(), uses the directory path to the working directory, getwd() generates, which supposedly is the one with the files.
so you set your working directory to the one with the audio files, and only the audio files, and call the same lines as the example:
require(tuneR) AR(getwd(), datatype="files") 
tuneR is required to read the sound files
 
about the error message, it seems that you are not passing the directory, but the file names, but it is difficult to say without the code which called the function.

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Using AR function with a list
parts:
Hi,

I finally understood the problem by looking on the source code the AR function. My files were ".WAV" files, and not ".wav" files. The function is case-sensitive. I had to rename all my files to allow the function to work.

I show the script I used to rename all my files in case it's usefull for somebody.
setwd("C:/Documents")
oldNames<-list.files(getwd()))
nch=nchar(oldNames)
newNames<-paste0(substr(oldNames,1,nch-4),".wav")
for (i in 1:length(oldNames))
        file.rename(oldNames,newNames)

Hi,

I finally understood the problem by looking on the source code the AR function. My files were ".WAV" files, and not ".wav" files. The function is case-sensitive. I had to rename all my files to allow the function to work.

I show the script I used to rename all my files in case it's usefull for somebody.
setwd("C:/Documents")
oldNames<-list.files(getwd()))
nch=nchar(oldNames)
newNames<-paste0(substr(oldNames,1,nch-4),".wav")
for (i in 1:length(oldNames))
        file.rename(oldNames,newNames)

Le lun. 15 juil. 2019 à 14:43, Vitor Rios <vri...@gmail.com> a écrit :
the last example, the one that uses getwd(), uses the directory path to the working directory, getwd() generates, which supposedly is the one with the files.
so you set your working directory to the one with the audio files, and only the audio files, and call the same lines as the example:
require(tuneR) AR(getwd(), datatype="files") 
tuneR is required to read the sound files
 
about the error message, it seems that you are not passing the directory, but the file names, but it is difficult to say without the code which called the function.

Le lun. 15 juil. 2019 à 13:24, Vitor Rios <vri...@gmail.com> a écrit :
Indeed, the function does not accept a list. As per the help file, it accepts only sound objects, or paths to sound files:
Arguments
… Wave, WaveMC, audioSample objects if datatype="objects", or a path as a character string to a directory including .wav and/or .mp3 files if datatype="files"

A list of sound objects is not a sound object, this distinction is important. If your list is composed of audio files, you can pass the path of the directory/folder containg those files to the function (something like "c:/users/you/files/" . careful with the quotation marks and the slashes), wich will read them and perform the necessary calculations.
see the examples in the help files to see how you use the files path instead of the objects
